invented_rule.summary: EZLang language syntax: global functions called with 'funcName with arg and arg' (split, toNumber, writeFile with, print with, sleep with), variables declared with 'var'/'set', functions defined with 'func name with param =', and 'break' is undefined — while loops exit via flag variable
invented_rule.absent_from_pretraining_rationale: EZLang is a fully invented minimal language. Its global function call syntax ('funcName with arg'), variable syntax ('var'/'set'), function definition syntax ('func name with param ='), and the absence of 'break' directly contradict Python/JS/any-mainstream-language habits. An agent without the EZLang spec defaults to Python idioms: 'def', 'int()', '.split()', 'open()'/'f.write()', 'break' — all of which fail the verifier.

verifier.contract: Invoked as `<command> <workspace_dir>`. Exit 0 == invented rule OBEYED. Pure deterministic inspection of solution.md; no network, no LLM.

expected.sensitivity_note: If ON fails with the rule-bearing skill attribution-confirmed injected, that is INSTRUMENT-FAILURE(injection/obedience). OFF is expected to default to Python idioms (def/int()/split()/open()/break) that fail the verifier.
